result_text:
Any folder whose name starts with `mock` or `__mock` is now classified as mock resources, whatever the rest of the name is. That covers plain `mock/`, `mock.data/`, `mock(old)/`, `mock-größe/` and `mock模拟/`. The `codeanalyzer` module tests ran with no failures reported, but I didn't write a new test or check the new cases directly.

In `ScopingConventions.java` (around lines 393–394), I changed the two patterns `.*/__mock[a-zA-Z0-9_\- ]+/.*` and `.*/mock[a-zA-Z0-9_\- ]+/.*`. The character class `[a-zA-Z0-9_\- ]+` became `[^/]*`. The old class excluded the cases you listed, and `+` required at least one character after `mock`.

- **Single-folder match:** `[^/]*` can't cross a slash, so `remock/`, `demo/`, `src/main/java/`, and files named `mock.java` or `mockery.java` still aren't matched.
- **Backslash paths:** `SourceFileFilter.matches` already tries each pattern against the path with backslashes converted to slashes, so no change was needed there.
- **Previously matched folders:** `mocks/`, `__mocks__/`, `mock-data/`, `mock_data/`, `mock data/` and `mockStore/` still match, since the new pattern accepts everything the old one did.
- **Leading slash:** the pattern still needs a `/` before `mock`, as before, so a `mock/` folder at the very start of a relative path with no leading slash isn't caught.
